scope: Read-only evidence and public API feasibility. No source/test proposal, compile/test/live execution, or Beads mutation.

owner.acceptance_criteria: Host/executor compile and preserve existing configuration precedence and refusal tests. Native probe states and actual runtime lifecycle failure are tested, including failure before first beat, listener termination, and bounded shutdown/flush. Report the public API limit: detection is bounded and the native hidden task error is available only through cleanup. Expose concrete shutdown bounds for deployment grace. Live NATS and operator recovery remain later deployed proof arms.

conclusion: Signals, bounded flush, native probe states, and supporting cleanup policy are exercised. First-beat failure of an actual native command task is still unexecuted; a deterministic public closed-client route is feasible. Real listener-to-native-runtime termination already passed upstream, but a WAMN executable failure path is not proved by those receipts.

acceptance_map.limit: Historical source receipts; root owns current scoped validation/final sweep.
Executor idle; host no guest workload.
Do not relabel injected pending cleanup as actual runtime termination or claim every plugin completed after timeout.

acceptance_map.claim: Cleanup is an opaque future whose first poll requests shutdown and whose completion returns the hidden task error. WAMN observes native liveness silence and public ingress stopped state beforehand; no hidden JoinHandle or private Ended enum is exposed.

acceptance_map.host: 61s envelope with 5s drain, seven plugins, native plugin stop default 5s, versus 70s grace. HTTP stop has only an outer allowance; timed-out cleanup stays failure.
acceptance_map.executor: 9s envelope (5s queue drain +1s probes +2s native flush +1s runtime shutdown), versus 15s grace.

gaps_and_feasibility.feasibility: clear through existing public APIs; no code prepared
route: Reuse the existing real NATS subprocess fixture. Connect a separate owned async-nats client and call its public drain().

Wait under a finite bound until subscribe on a valid test subject returns the public closed-send failure. drain() itself only queues closure; do not treat its return, server outage, or disconnected state as proof the client command channel is closed.

Pass that confirmed closed client to native ClusterHostBuilder::with_nats_client and attach native Liveness. Use a nonzero heartbeat interval through with_heartbeat_interval, derive the silence budget with liveness_silence, and retain ProbeState.
Start a release-less ClusterHost without ingress/plugins/workloads. start() can return successfully because it spawns the subscribe task; that task then fails before the first liveness.beat.

Run the actual public WAMN watch_liveness after start returns, without polling cleanup. Require the first-beat error within the configured silence budget plus polling margin, silence()==None, and no started transition. A real native probe socket can record ready starting/live ok while waiting.

Only after watcher failure, mark drain and pass the real opaque cleanup future to public bounded_cleanup. Require Err, with subscribe context available via the public cleanup result; keep the hidden native task inaccessible.
Drop the returned HostApi handle and retained native objects, shut down/join owned probe task if used, and stop/reap only the existing owned NATS child.
gaps_and_feasibility.why_it_is_a_real_failure: Native ClusterHost async subscribe fails on its actual closed command channel; neither the liveness observer nor a synthetic beat/failure future creates that failure.
limits: This is an in-process native ClusterHost plus production WAMN lifecycle helpers. It does not inject a closed client into the wamn-host executable.
A reduced, public builder heartbeat interval proves the configured 3x silence rule; it does not measure default 45-second behavior. Use the default if that wall-clock bound is required.
Native subscribe failure returns before Host::stop. Keep this fixture release-less with no ingress/plugins/workloads and drop its owned handles; do not claim plugin cleanup completed.

gaps_and_feasibility.feasibility: clear native public route; WAMN process route unavailable without a separate owner change
route: Reuse the existing real NATS fixture. Build native Ingress on an owned ephemeral loopback port, retain its ConnectionLimit and Arc, and install it on ClusterHostBuilder along with Liveness.
Require a real command-loop beat/heartbeat RPC and an actual ingress response before inducing failure.

Call the retained Ingress public HostHandler::stop without polling ClusterHost cleanup. Await ConnectionLimit::stopped and require accepting=false and unrecoverable=true. This closes the actual accept loop and activates the same native guard as an accept error or panic.
Observe native API termination before polling cleanup, as the already-passing upstream test does; separately the actual WAMN watch_liveness can detect that real command loop becoming stale.
Use WAMN bounded_cleanup only after the observed failure. The native cleanup result must remain an error naming ingress, even if shutdown races the stop.
Stop/join owned probe listener and drop owned native handles; reuse existing NATS exact-child cleanup.
limits: WAMN ingress_stopped/stop_after are private to the binary host module. An existing host-module unit test could compose them with a real Ingress, but the integration test cannot call them without an owner change; do not duplicate the production supervisor just to claim coverage.
The existing integration owner can exercise public WAMN watch_liveness/bounded_cleanup plus real native objects, and must label that scope accurately.

Native probe serve has a public shutdown future; terminating that real owned task is possible, but the existing WAMN executable does not expose its JoinSet/stop handle externally. It does not create a full-process failure route.

facts: wamn-host creates its own scheduler client and native ingress, then drops external access to their handles. It exposes no RPC for stopping its HTTP handler or draining its internal control client.

Stopping the external NATS server is a reconnect/outage proof; native loop continues beating. A permission-denied SUB is an asynchronous NATS event and must not be assumed to return subscribe Err before the beat.
A conflicting bind address is synchronous startup refusal, not a detached native command task failing after startup returns.
No fault flags, global FD exhaustion, synthetic heartbeat, copied runtime, private native error surface, or second harness is proposed.
black_box_boundary.decision_scope: The exact acceptance can gain direct native-failure evidence through existing public WAMN lifecycle helpers in the current test owner. A claim about the full executable unexpected-failure branch would remain explicitly unproved; do not invent an extra production interface for it.
